_comment: Reviewed classification of every real-wall-clock (Date.now) caller observed inside decision modules during a synthetic session (2026-10-13, scripts/sim/wallClockCheck.ts). SIM_SEAMED = reads a simulation/replay clock seam when SYNTHETIC_SIMULATION/replay is active. LATENCY_ONLY = elapsed-time measurement, never a market-time decision. ID_OR_LOG_ONLY = identifier or log/ring-buffer timestamp. REAL_TIME_BY_DESIGN = compares wall-clock stamps with wall-clock stamps created in the same process (idea freshness, rate limits, circuit-breaker cooldowns) so simulated vs real time cannot disagree; the only effect is that those windows elapse in real rather than simulated time. A NEW caller not listed here fails certification until it is reviewed and classified.

classifications.reason: nowMs() reads the simulation clock installed by SyntheticSessionEngine (2026-10-13)
diagnostic capturedAtMs stamp; priceAgeMs inside it uses the seamed getLatestPriceAgeMs
cooldown clock uses replay.clock.now() when a replay session is active (TechnicalAgent.ts nowForCooldown)
the simulated clock itself derives simulated time from real elapsed time x speed
event/log/ring-buffer timestamps, ids and stage timers
HTTP latency, circuit-breaker cooldown and request stamps toward the local Java service; bar timestamps sent to Java come from the revealed synthetic bars, not these reads
per-symbol prediction cooldown and model re-check interval are real-time rate limits (fidelity note: at accelerated speed they allow fewer forecasts per simulated minute than live)
evaluation timing / last-evaluated stamps used for scheduling bounds, not for bar or quote freshness
idea receivedAt and freshness windows are stamped and compared on the same wall clock
request pacing / rate-limit back-off / cache TTL for real provider calls; synthetic sessions serve bars from the injected provider
exit-idea emission throttle (canEmitPortfolioExitIdea) and timing; position price freshness is measured by the seamed MarketDataWorker age
TTL pruning, history stamps, bounded waits and interval guards measured against the same wall clock
